summary: The paper presents a spectral approach to vectorless 3D thermal integrity verification for microprocessors using graph signal processing, spectral sparsification, and multilevel frameworks. The scenario describes two experimental microprocessor designs (Processor A: 28W, 195mm², 4 metal/11 material layers; Processor B: 50W, 302mm², 6 metal/15 material layers) analyzed under worst-case power density constraints without explicit workload vectors. The paper uses steady-state linear thermal models solved via Cholesky decomposition and Gurobi LP optimization, reporting relative errors of 1–5% across seven test cases (T1–T7 ranging from 25k to 2M thermal grid nodes). Studio did not run because the scenario is marked not_2d_applicable: the experiment definition lacks a floorplan (1–128 blocks required) and empty power_w dictionary. The 2D screening label is correctly assigned as 'not_2d_applicable' because the paper addresses inherently 3D thermal grid analysis with multi-layer material structures and full 3D mesh discretization, not 2D planar transient dynamics. No transient trace is expected since the work focuses on steady-state worst-case temperature distributions via constraint satisfaction rather than time-domain thermal transients. No comparison with Studio results is valid.
limitations: Studio did not execute due to missing floorplan block definitions and power consumption dictionary—custom 2D steady experiments require 1–128 named blocks with corresponding power_w entries in watts

The scenario describes full 3D thermal grid methods fundamentally incompatible with 2D steady-state screening; spectral sparsification and multilevel AMG frameworks operate on 3D nodal Laplacian eigenvalue spectra, not 2D rectangular meshes

Physical mismatches include vectorless constraint-based analysis (no actual workload vectors), steady-state only (no transient dynamics), linear thermal superposition (no temperature-dependent properties), and spectral approximation that discards high-frequency spatial modes

Critical inputs missing: exact 3D geometry files, complete thermal conductivity for all 11–15 material layers, detailed boundary conditions, power distribution maps, workload-to-power mapping, algorithm parameters (ε_th, β), LP solver tolerances, and baseline comparisons for relative assessment

Extracted evidence lacks valid asset pinning; no independent verification of reported relative errors (1–5%) against a canonical reference thermal solver or against the paper's own fine-grid full-system solutions

Comparison is not valid because the 3D multilevel vectorless method and hypothetical Studio 2D steady results operate on incompatible geometries, optimization regimes (LP-based worst-case vs. deterministic power map), and aggregation levels (global spectral modes vs. local block steady-state)
The paper does not provide transient temperature traces, circuit-level thermal coupling, or time-domain verification data required for comprehensive transient thermal integrity assessment
